title: Sleep in Psychosomatic Inpatients
summary:
Background:
Sleep problems are a very common accompanying symptom in people with mental health conditions. From our own previous surveys, we know that about 76% of patients treated in a specialized clinic for psychosomatics (tertiary care) suffer from at least one form of sleep disorder. To date, however, German clinics for psychosomatics have not systematically and precisely investigated the specific types of sleep disorders involved. There is often a lack of objective sleep measurements and insights into exactly how sleep is connected to specific conditions — such as somatic symptom disorders, depression, anxiety disorders, or trauma-related disorders.

Objectives:
The study investigates how frequently and in what form sleep disorders occur in patients undergoing inpatient psychosomatic treatment. We want to find out how objective sleep data, daytime activity, personal dream experiences, and mental health are interconnected. Additionally, the study will examine whether and how sleep changes as a result of the multi-week hospital treatment.

Methodology:
The study starts on June 30, 2026, and will run for three years. The goal is to include at least 100 adult patients (m/f/d) receiving inpatient treatment at the Department of Psychosomatics and Psychotherapy at the University Hospital Cologne. Participation is voluntary and requires written informed consent.

To obtain a comprehensive picture, sleep will be assessed in two ways at the beginning (week of admission) and towards the end (treatment week 8) of the stay:

 Objective measurements: Sleep is measured somnographically and non-invasively at night directly in the patient's room. During the day, physical activity is recorded via a wrist sensor.

Subjective assessments: In addition to clinical routine, participants fill out scientific questionnaires regarding their sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and mental health. During their hospital stay, they also keep a daily sleep and dream diary.

All collected data will be stored securely and pseudonymized in strict compliance with data protection regulations, and evaluated in cooperation with the Institute of Medical Statistics and Bioinformatics.

Expected Benefit:
Upon completion of the study, we hope to have a clearer picture of how severely patients in tertiary psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic care are affected by sleep disorders. In the future, these findings should help us better understand the interactions between sleep and the psyche, allowing us to tailor therapeutic interventions more precisely and improve patient care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient admission for complex psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic treatment at the Department of Psychosomatics and Psychotherapy, University Hospital Cologne.

Sufficient knowledge of the German language to independently complete the study questionnaires.

Willingness to participate in the study and provision of written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute somatic diseases that require transfer to another medical department or hospital.

Presence of severe psychiatric disorders (e.g., acute psychosis, acute suicidality) that make participation in the study impossible.

Cognitive impairments that prevent comprehension of the study contents and completion of the questionnaires.

Insufficient reading skills or inadequate knowledge of the German language.
